scale.name: Not bootable
scale.meaning: A clean checkout can't install, build and pass its tests.

scale.name: Bootable
scale.meaning: A clean checkout installs, builds and passes every test.

scale.name: Verifiable
scale.meaning: Agents can check their own work: the commands pass, the tests catch planted faults, the instructions are accurate and normal work needs no production access.

scale.name: Delegable
scale.meaning: Agent PRs meet the outcome targets your team set, over at least 20 agent PRs in the window (never fewer than 10).

scale.name: Scalable
scale.meaning: Those targets held over two back-to-back windows while agent PR volume at least doubled.

executive.nextLine: Next: Level 3, delegable. It needs outcome targets your team sets and agent PRs that meet them: no Level 3 targets are recorded.
executive.ask: Decision needed: the merge rate, first-time CI pass rate and review load that mean agents handle work here. Also name an owner for agent readiness.
executive.coverage: The level covers 1 component. Listed for review, not blocking: host mode was allowed on a Cursor Cloud Agent VM, detected by /exec-daemon and CLOUD_AGENT_INJECTED_SECRET_NAMES: the repo's commands ran on that machine as its user, outside a container, with a throwaway home and no account credentials; they could read its local files, which a disposable VM holds only for this run, and the secrets injected into it. A pass there proves the VM as provisioned, including its preinstalled tools and running services, which a clean container may not have.

checks.name: Setup works from a clean checkout
checks.why: Every agent starts from a clean checkout, so setup that only works on a prepared machine breaks every agent run.

sources.claim: In the BootstrapAgent study, a reusable, verified setup cut later agents' token use by 25.9% and build time by 22.3%.
sources.caveat: Measured on the study's benchmark repositories.

checks.name: Build, lint, type-check and test commands pass
checks.why: Agents need one known way to check their own work, and a type-check counts only once the audit has seen it fail on a type error it planted.

checks.name: Tests catch planted faults
checks.why: Green tests aren't proof that a change is right.

sources.claim: OpenAI estimated about 30% of SWE-Bench Pro's 731 public tasks were broken, including low-coverage tests that let incomplete fixes pass.
sources.caveat: An audit of one benchmark, not of customer repositories.

checks.name: Agent instructions are accurate
checks.why: Agents follow AGENTS.md, rules and skills literally, so a stale command costs more than a missing one. No outcome study yet measures how much these files help.

checks.name: Normal work needs no production access
checks.why: Agents run with whatever access setup gives them, so normal work must never need production credentials.
